title: Understanding temperature
body: Air temperature measures how warm or cold the air is, usually in degrees Celsius. It changes with time of day, season, cloud cover, altitude and location.

title: What is humidity?
body: Relative humidity compares the water vapour in the air with the most the air can hold at that temperature. High humidity makes warm weather feel heavier and more uncomfortable.

title: Wind speed and weather
body: Wind speed tells you how fast air is moving. Strong winds can disrupt travel, damage trees and buildings, and make outdoor activities unsafe. Follow official warnings in severe weather.

title: Understanding rainfall
body: Rain falls when water droplets in clouds grow heavy enough to drop. Rainfall measurements help with water management and flood monitoring.

title: Flood awareness
body: Heavy or prolonged rain can cause flooding. Never walk or drive through floodwater, because its depth and current are hard to judge. Follow local emergency instructions.

title: Thunderstorm safety
body: During a thunderstorm, go inside a sturdy building or a closed vehicle. Stay away from open areas, isolated trees and water. Wait until the storm has passed before going back out.

title: Forecasts and uncertainty
body: Forecasts combine observations with numerical models to estimate future conditions. Accuracy drops the further ahead you look, so check updated official forecasts before important decisions.

title: The Indian monsoon
body: The Indian summer monsoon brings seasonal rain to much of the country. Timing and intensity vary by region and year, so consult IMD forecasts and alerts when planning around heavy rain.
